graph.title: LED Matrix Row-Column Scanning
notes: Matrix row/column to Arduino pin mapping follows the manual's table (Row1=2, Row2=7, Row3=A5, Row4=5, Row5=13, Row6=A4, Row7=12, Row8=A2; Col1=6, Col2=11, Col3=10, Col4=3, Col5=A3, Col6=4, Col7=8, Col8=9). Matrix ports R1-R8 and C1-C8 are used as the catalogue's row/column pins.

The 8 resistors sit on the yellow wires, which are the digital pins 2-9 in the image. Each resistor lead 1 plugs into the Arduino header and lead 2 is joined to a yellow jumper wire that goes to the matrix. The image shows no breadboard for these resistors.
The 1k resistors use value=1000, which is a prop value I chose.

The pots straddle the breadboard centre gap in the image. I assumed SIG on the left (bank t, row e) and GND/VCC on the right (bank b, column f). Their wires go to the right-hand power rails. I took 'bp' as the + rail and 'bn' as the - rail, and the rail hole numbers are approximate.
Pot 1 (upper, rows 8-10) is wired to A1 and pot 2 (lower, rows 14-16) to A0, following the blue wires in the image.
The black wire from the Arduino goes to the upper GND header pin, which I took to be GND.2.

breadboard.name: Solderless breadboard
breadboard.port_rule: Holes are named '<column><bank>.<row>': column 1-30, bank 't' (top half, rows a-e) or 'b' (bottom half, rows f-j), e.g. '12t.c', '7b.h'. The 5 holes of one column-bank are one strip. Power rails: 'tp.<n>', 'tn.<n>', 'bp.<n>', 'bn.<n>' (each rail is one strip).
